Database.doc: In-memory table catalog. Holds a list of named tables and (v6) a parallel views registry. Tables and views are inserted by the caller via `database_install_table` / `database_install_view` before the VDBE runs; the VDBE reads + writes tables, but only reads views (views are compile-time-resolved). Pin 18 (v8-pager): `pager` field carries the page-cache + WAL state owned by `/parts/storage/parts/wal-bridge`. In-memory mode constructs the Pager via `pager_new_in_memory()` and consults it without doing I/O; path-backed mode (open_database_at) assigns a `JournalMode::Wal` Pager. Cloning a Database produces a fresh in-memory Pager regardless of the source's mode (P18.4) — path-backed databases are constructed via `open_database_at`, never via `Clone`. This codifies the existing semantics that LockManager + WAL writer state are not cloneable; a clone is a new logical instance, not a duplicated handle on the source's on-disk artifacts.

DatabaseTablesView.doc: Pin 18 (v8-pager): companion view exposing mutable references to every Database field EXCEPT `pager`. Returned by `Database::split_pager_mut` alongside `&mut Pager` so VDBE opcode handlers can hold both borrows simultaneously without conflicting `&mut Database`. The disjoint-borrow guarantee is essential for cursor write paths that mutate rows AND consult the pager (B-tree page faulting in pin 19+; cursor-threading in 18.1c). Targets emit the helper using their natural idiom: Rust uses field-destructuring of `&mut Database`; C uses struct-field pointer aliasing; Zig uses separate `*` fields; Go uses separate fields; Python uses paired attribute references (no aliasing model — the contract is that mutations through one do not invalidate the other).

MemTable.doc: One named table: its name, optional column-name list (for UPDATE name→index resolution), the rows in insertion order, and a parallel rowids vector (v5). Column arity is whatever the caller stored — the VDBE resolves columns by index supplied by the Column opcode. If column_names is empty, UPDATE by name will fail with SchemaMissing; INSERT/SELECT/DELETE do not consult column_names. rowids[i] is the SQLite-style 1-based rowid of rows[i]; cursor_insert_row appends rows[i].len()+1 by default but accepts an explicit-rowid path when column_names contains a 'rowid' entry. v7-pp: indexes is a (possibly empty) list of IndexSpec entries describing per-table indexes available to the planner. v1 only ever emits a single `Rowid` index (corresponding to the table's INTEGER PRIMARY KEY column, when the schema declares one). `Unique` and `NonUnique` are reserved for follow-up parts (storage/index, btree-backed) and MUST NOT be populated by mem-store callers in v1. The field is optional in the sense that v1 callers that don't install an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY MAY leave it as the empty list; existing callers that don't yet emit an indexes field continue to round-trip via target-side default-empty initialization. Pin 16-amend (2026-04-27): `pk_col_name` mirrors the column name of the `Rowid` IndexSpec (when present) for O(1) UPDATE-by-name resolution. `database_install_table_with_pk` sets it to `Some(name)`; `database_install_table` leaves it `None`. Targets emit it as a public optional-string field. Pin 16-amend (2026-04-27): `pk_index` is an auxiliary rowid → RowLocation map maintained alongside `rowids` so `cursor_seek_rowid` is O(log N) instead of O(N). Logically rowid → RowLocation { InMemory { row_index } | Paged { page_no, cell_index } }; today only the InMemory variant is populated, Paged is reserved for pin 19.1 cursor migration. Targets choose the concrete container (Rust `Rc<RefCell<BTreeMap<i64, RowLocation>>>`, Python dict, Go map, etc.) and the concrete RowLocation representation (Rust enum, C tagged union, Python tuple+sentinel, Go interface, Zig `union(enum)`). The contract is that lookups are sub-linear in the row count and the map stays consistent with `rowids` after every insert/delete/update for in-memory mode; path-backed tables MAY leave pk_index empty in pin 19a (cursor falls through to legacy linear scan) until pin 19.1 populates the `Paged` variant. The `cursor_seek_rowid` body MUST consult this map; direct external reads are permitted but the recommended access path is `database_clone_table` (deep-copy snapshot) or `cursor_seek_rowid` (single-rowid query). The schema field type remains `map<i64, u32>` as documented prose for in-memory variant carrying `row_index`; targets implementing the path-backed `Paged` variant promote the value to a target-native sum type per the Pin 19a amendment in master.md.

IndexKind.doc: v7-pp: classifies an index. Only `Rowid` is honored by v1 mem-store; the other two are placeholders for the storage/index and storage/btree parts. The compiler's predicate-pushdown rule (see /parts/compiler/parts/predicate-pushdown) consults a `Rowid` entry to recognise an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY table.

Rowid.doc: The table's INTEGER PRIMARY KEY column. The single column entry in `IndexSpec.columns` is the 0-based column index of that PK column. SeekRowid (parts/vdbe/parts/opcodes-rows) takes a value of that column and positions the cursor at the matching row.

Unique.doc: Reserved for follow-up. v1 mem-store MUST NOT emit this kind.

NonUnique.doc: Reserved for follow-up. v1 mem-store MUST NOT emit this kind.

IndexSpec.doc: v7-pp: declares one index over a MemTable. `kind` discriminates the index family (see IndexKind). `columns` is the list of 0-based column indices that form the index key; for `Rowid` exactly one entry is permitted (the INTEGER PRIMARY KEY column). For v1 mem-store, the only legal shape is `IndexSpec { kind: Rowid, columns: [pk_col_index] }` and at most one such entry per MemTable.

ViewEntry.doc: v6 view registry entry. Stores the view name plus the original SELECT text; the compiler re-tokenizes + re-parses on each reference (views are resolved as synthetic derived-table sources, never mutate the tables array). Cycle detection lives in the compiler.

TableSnapshot.doc: v7-tx (pin 17): one entry of a transaction stack frame, capturing the rollback-restorable extent of one MemTable at BEGIN time. `rows_len` is the number of rows present at the snapshot moment; `rowids_len` is the parallel rowids vector length (always equal to rows_len in well-formed states, but recorded separately because the two vectors are stored independently and the rollback path truncates each to its own snapshot length). On ROLLBACK every table is truncated to its corresponding snapshot lengths; tables installed AFTER BEGIN (i.e. not present in the snapshot frame) are left untouched in v1 — DDL inside a transaction is out of scope. v1 limitation: snapshots only restore length, NOT individual row content. UPDATE and DELETE inside a transaction therefore CANNOT be rolled back faithfully in v1. The L4 INSERT-only workload that motivates this leaf is correctly handled.

TxnFrame.doc: v7-tx (pin 17): one transaction stack frame. v1 mem-store admits only a single active frame at a time (no nested savepoints), but the structure is a list-of-frames so a future SAVEPOINT extension does not need a shape change. `tables` records one TableSnapshot per Database table that existed at BEGIN time, in the table-array order at BEGIN time.

CursorHandle.doc: Cursor over a MemTable's rows. Each cursor stores a reference to its table such that writes through `cursor_insert_row` are visible to other cursors opened on the same Database (targets implement this via shared-mutability — Rc<RefCell<>> in Rust, pointer-into-Database in C, etc.). Position `u32::MAX` (or target-equivalent 'not positioned') means 'before first row' (fresh cursor) or 'past last row' (exhausted). The caller MUST call cursor_rewind before cursor_column.

database_new.doc: Construct an empty Database (zero tables, zero views, empty txn_stack). Pin 18 (v8-pager): also initializes `pager` via `pager_new_in_memory()` per /parts/storage/parts/wal-bridge — the freshly constructed Database has `journal_mode == Memory` and `synchronous == Off`. Path-backed Pagers are produced by `open_database_at` (fileformat-read leaf) and assigned into the Database after construction; `database_new()` itself never touches a path. Callers install tables via database_install_table.

split_pager_mut.doc: Pin 18 (v8-pager): borrow-split helper. Returns disjoint mutable borrows of `(DatabaseTablesView, Pager)` so callers can hold a &mut Pager and a &mut tables view simultaneously. Targets that express disjoint-mutable-references in safe code (Rust) emit a destructuring of &mut Database; targets without an aliasing model (Python, Go) emit a structurally-equivalent pair of attribute references — the contract is that mutations through the view do not invalidate the Pager and vice-versa. Used by VDBE opcode handlers in pin 18.1c (cursor signature migration) and by every commit-bridge call site that needs both surfaces. The function is a method on Database in language idioms that support method syntax; in idioms that don't (C), it is a free function `database_split_pager_mut(db_ptr) -> (view_ptr, pager_ptr)`.

database_install_table.doc: Install a named table with the provided rows and column-name list. Replaces any existing table with the same name (case-sensitive match for the probe; case-insensitive SQL-semantic match is deferred to the real storage part). column_names may be empty; if empty, UPDATE by name will fail with SchemaMissing at runtime. INSERT/SELECT/DELETE do not consult column_names. Returns unit. Equivalent to `database_install_table_with_pk` with `pk_column = None`.

database_install_table_with_pk.doc: First-class entrypoint for installing a table that may have a rowid-alias INTEGER PRIMARY KEY column. Same semantics as `database_install_table` plus an optional `pk_column` naming the rowid-alias column. When `pk_column` is `Some(name)`, the storage MUST: (1) resolve `name` against `column_names` (ASCII-case-insensitive match); (2) record the resolved 0-based index on the MemTable as a `Rowid` IndexSpec (`IndexSpec { kind: Rowid, columns: [resolved_index] }`); (3) set `MemTable.pk_col_name = Some(name)` per pin 16-amend; (4) use that column's INTEGER value as the rowid for subsequent `cursor_insert_row` calls (mirroring SQLite's rowid-alias semantics). When `pk_column` is `None`, no IndexSpec is installed and `pk_col_name` is left `None` (auto-rowid behavior). If `pk_column` is `Some` but the name does not appear in `column_names`, behavior is undefined for v1 — callers MUST validate against the schema before calling (the parser-leaf helper `pk_from_create_stmt` only returns names of columns it has seen). Replace-on-conflict semantics match the no-pk variant.

open_read_cursor.doc: Open a read cursor on the named table. Returns err(TableNotFound) if the table is not installed. The returned cursor is NOT positioned on any row; the caller must call cursor_rewind first.

close_cursor.doc: Release a cursor. In-memory implementation is a no-op (no file handles); exists to match the stable storage interface.

cursor_rewind.doc: Position the cursor on the first row of the table. Returns Ok(true) if the table has at least one row; Ok(false) if the table is empty (the cursor is marked not-valid and subsequent cursor_column will error). Pin 18.1c (2026-04-27): takes `pager: &mut Pager` per the wal-bridge contract — pin 18.1c is structural; pin 19 (`parts/storage/parts/btree-write/master.md`) routes path-backed reads through `pager_get_page` via this parameter.

cursor_next.doc: Advance the cursor to the next row. Returns Ok(true) if another row is available and the cursor is now on it; Ok(false) if the previous row was the last (cursor becomes not-valid). Precondition: cursor must currently be valid (rewound and not exhausted). Pin 18.1c (2026-04-27): takes `pager: &mut Pager`.

cursor_column.doc: Read a column value from the row the cursor currently points at. col_index is 0-based within the row. Returns err(InvalidCursor) if the cursor is not positioned on a row, and err(IoError) for out-of-range col_index (the probe does not distinguish types of range error). Pin 18.1c (2026-04-27): takes `pager: &mut Pager` (NOT &Pager — page-cache pin 3 makes LRU touch a mutation; the wal-bridge `pager_get_page` signature is borrow_mut to match).

open_write_cursor.doc: Open a write-capable cursor on the named table. Same return semantics as `open_read_cursor` — not positioned on any row until caller rewinds or inserts. For the probe, write cursors and read cursors share one representation; the distinction is only by API entry point.

cursor_insert_row.doc: Append a new row to the cursor's table. If column_names is Some, its length equals values.len() and each name corresponds positionally to values[i] (the caller has already validated this against the table's schema); the row stored is built by starting from an all-Null row of the schema's width and writing each named value into its index — for the probe, column_names is passed through untouched because the smoke uses no-column-list INSERTs primarily. If column_names is None, values is stored directly as the row (the caller has validated arity against the schema). Returns the new rowid (the 1-based position in the table after the append). Cursor position is NOT advanced by this call. Pin 18.1c (2026-04-27): takes `pager: &mut Pager`. Row-vector mutation still flows through interior mutability on MemTable (Rc<RefCell<>> in Rust); the pager param is structural — pin 19 (`parts/storage/parts/btree-write/master.md`) routes the page write through it.

cursor_delete_row.doc: Remove the row the cursor currently points at. Precondition: cursor is valid. After deletion, the cursor is placed such that a subsequent `cursor_next` call returns true iff there was a row AFTER the deleted one (without skipping it). In practice: remove rows[row_index]; if row_index was 0, set row_index to sentinel `u32::MAX` meaning 'before first' (so cursor_next advances to index 0 of the now-shifted table); else, decrement row_index by 1 (so cursor_next's +1 lands on the row that shifted into the deleted slot). Pin 18.1c (2026-04-27): takes `pager: &mut Pager`.

cursor_seek_rowid.doc: v5: position the cursor at the row whose rowid equals the given i64. Returns Ok(true) if a row with that rowid exists (cursor.is_valid = true, row_index points at the matching row); Ok(false) if no row matches (cursor becomes not-valid). Pin 16-amend (2026-04-27): consults pk_index for sub-linear lookup. Pin 18.1c (2026-04-27): takes `pager: &mut Pager`.

database_install_view.doc: v6: install or replace a view by name. select_sql is the original SELECT text; the compiler re-parses it at each reference. ASCII-case-insensitive replace-on-conflict (last-write-wins). Name collisions with installed tables are caller-policed; storage does not check.

database_drop_view.doc: v6: drop a view by name (ASCII-case-insensitive). Returns true if a matching view was removed, false if no view by that name existed (caller chooses whether missing-view DROP is silent or an error).

database_lookup_view.doc: v6: read-only fetch of a view entry by name (ASCII-case-insensitive). Returns Some(entry) if installed, None otherwise.

database_begin_transaction.doc: v7-tx (pin 17): open a new transaction. Capture a TableSnapshot (rows_len, rowids_len) for every currently-installed table, push the resulting TxnFrame onto db.txn_stack. v1 mem-store admits at most one active frame: if `txn_stack` is already non-empty, return err(IoError) — re-BEGIN inside an active transaction is a caller error. The current values of `rows`, `rowids`, and `pk_index` (target-local) are NOT cloned — only the lengths are recorded. Subsequent inserts append; rollback truncates back to the recorded length. UPDATE/DELETE rollback fidelity is OUT OF SCOPE for v1 (see TableSnapshot doc).

database_commit_transaction.doc: v7-tx (pin 17): commit the most recent transaction frame. Pop the top entry of `db.txn_stack` and discard it — the current rows/rowids state becomes permanent. If `txn_stack` is empty (no active transaction), return err(IoError). v1 only supports a single-level transaction; commit clears the stack to empty.

database_rollback_transaction.doc: v7-tx (pin 17): roll back the most recent transaction frame. Pop the top entry of `db.txn_stack`. For every TableSnapshot in that frame (identified by `table_index`), truncate `tables[table_index].rows` and `tables[table_index].rowids` back to the recorded lengths. Targets MUST also synchronize any auxiliary state derived from the row vector (e.g. the pk_index used by cursor_seek_rowid) so post-rollback queries do not see ghost entries. v1 limitation: only INSERTs are correctly rolled back — UPDATE in-place mutations and DELETE-then-INSERT sequences are NOT restored to their pre-transaction values (the snapshot only records lengths). If `txn_stack` is empty, return err(IoError).

cursor_update_row.doc: Update specific columns of the row the cursor currently points at. column_names names which columns to overwrite; values[i] corresponds to column_names[i]. Length invariant: column_names.len() == values.len(). Names are resolved to indices via the table's stored column_names (MemTable.column_names). Name not found → err(SchemaMissing). Table has empty column_names → err(SchemaMissing). (Existing emissions before 2026-04-24 may still fall back to IoError — propagating the new variant to 5 targets is a follow-up.) Any matched slot is overwritten; unlisted slots are unchanged. Cursor position is NOT modified. Pin 18.1c (2026-04-27): takes `pager: &mut Pager`.

database_clone_table.doc: Pin 16-amend (2026-04-27): produce an owned deep-copy of the named MemTable, materializing its rows / rowids / pk_index / pk_col_name without sharing reference-counted state with the source. Used by /parts/storage/parts/backup-engine to capture a snapshot that does not alias the source database — without this method, the backup engine would have to reach into pk_index / rows / rowids directly and clone-out each container, leaking target-private representations. Returns err(TableNotFound) if no table by that name exists. Behavioral contract: subsequent writes to the source MemTable MUST NOT be visible through the returned clone.
